acceptance.criterion_verbatim: A pre-migration user logs in successfully AND reads a DEFINED MFA preference. Evidence: the user's pre-migration state, then the post-migration read-back showing a non-null value. A schema dump is not this.
acceptance.invocation: (a) DynamoDB scan of every SK=PROFILE item BEFORE the backfill; (b) a controlled account written in the PRE-MIGRATION SHAPE (no mfa attributes at all); (c) 005_backfill_mfa_defaults.py --apply; (d) POST /auth/login then GET /auth/me against the deployed API.
acceptance.output_evidence: PRE: 48 of 48 PROFILE items carried NO mfaChannel and NO phoneNumber; the controlled account read hasOwnProperty(mfaChannel)=false, raw value undefined. POST: login status=200 hasAccessToken=true; GET /auth/me -> mfaChannel="none", mfaEnabled=false. Population after: 49 of 49 DEFINED.
acceptance.denominator: 48 PROFILE items of 75 total table items pre-migration (scan paginated to exhaustion; 1 page, LastEvaluatedKey absent); 49 after the controlled account was added.
acceptance.status_reason: The LOGIN half was exercised on an account CREATED in the pre-migration shape rather than on one of the original 48, because this seat holds no password for any of those 48. Stated rather than glossed: the FIELD half is measured on the real population, the LOGIN half on a faithful synthetic.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: A WRONG code is rejected. Name the code submitted.
acceptance.output_evidence: status=401 {"error":"Invalid or expired code"}. Handler log: {"event":"mfa_code_rejected","reason":"wrong_code","attempts":1}. THE CODE SUBMITTED WAS 000000; the live code at that moment was 084699.
acceptance.denominator: 1 wrong-code submission against a live, unexpired challenge.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: A REPLAYED (previously-valid, already-consumed) code is rejected. This is the one most often skipped and the one that matters -- a replayable OTP is not a second factor.
acceptance.invocation: POST /auth/mfa/verify {challengeId:'dd8ed4aba596b3d5371c39d7e241a965', code:'084699'} submitted TWICE, byte-identical requests, back to back.
acceptance.output_evidence: 1st: status=200, accessToken issued, refresh cookie set. 2nd (replay of the now-consumed code): status=401 {"error":"Invalid or expired code"}. Single use is enforced by DeleteItem + ConditionExpression attribute_exists(pk), so a replay finds nothing to consume.
acceptance.denominator: 2 identical submissions of one previously-valid code; the ONLY variable is ordering.
acceptance.status_reason: The two requests are byte-identical, so the 401 is caused by consumption and not by a malformed request -- the first call is its own control.

Time-constant sweep, stated exhaustively so none hides: NEW in this work = CHALLENGE_TTL_SEC=600 (declared CHOSEN in-source, not measured) with CHALLENGE_TTL_MINUTES DERIVED from it, plus ttl=300 on the four Route53 records (a DNS cache TTL, a different quantity). Subject '084699 is your Opal Invest login code', receivedDateTime 2026-09-01T00:15:49Z, from noreply@opalinvest.dev, body legible with the code rendered, links rewritten by the tenant's Avanan gateway. The code READ FROM THAT MAILBOX was then submitted and ACCEPTED (200) by the deployed handler -- so the delivered message is provably the live challenge, not a lookalike.

acceptance.status_reason: DELIVERY IS PROVEN; THE FOLDER IS NOT, AND I WILL NOT CLAIM IT. The gateway tools available to this seat (list_recent_email / search_email / read_email) return no parentFolderId and are not folder-scoped, so I cannot discriminate Inbox from Junk on my own instrument. Claiming 'inbox' from a successful search would be exactly the unearned half of this criterion. Andrew's own view of the mailbox settles it in one look, and the SPF + DMARC + custom MAIL FROM records this TO landed are the reason to expect Inbox.

declared_exclusions.item: Cell 2.5 -- per-account MFA enablement as a separate build
declared_exclusions.reason: NOT BUILT, DELIBERATELY, and section 5 of the TO invited exactly this answer. The staged-rollout ordering Andrew stated is satisfiable WITHOUT it: cell 1.1's per-user mfaChannel/mfaEnabled fields ARE per-account enablement, and cell 1.2 leaves every account at 'none' (OFF). No client account can be exposed to MFA until someone deliberately flips that account, and Andrew's own account was enabled by a single item write. Building 2.5 would have been scope invented on an inference its own author flagged as not-Andrew's-words.
